concept: multiplication as equal groups and arrays, connected to skip-counting and interpreted in word problems
selectionReason:
Scenario 1 is the only candidate that reaches substantive interactive content at all, and it has the highest scores across every dimension (design 3, originality 2, craft 3, functionality 3, learning integration 3, replay 2), versus scenario 2 which never leaves its splash screen (confirmed non-functional across three separate progression attempts, scoring 1s across nearly every axis) and scenario 3 which is a fully functional but generically structured multiple-choice quiz with an actual state-management bug (recycled feedback text misreporting the previous question's numbers).

While scenario 1's interactions are criticized as passive 'reveal' sequences rather than true manipulables, and one '+' control appears unresponsive, the pedagogical sequencing (equal groups → skip-counting → arrays) is sound, the array grid is genuinely laid out as rows/columns, and the art is coherent and legible. Critically, this candidate has real, if shallow, gameplay to diagnose and refine — there's an actual mechanic (even if it needs to become more active/tactile) to iterate on, unlike scenario 2 which offers nothing to refine (a broken shell) or scenario 3 which is confirmed to be a static answer-quiz with no path toward becoming a manipulable mechanic without a full rebuild.

Given the task is to select the candidate with the most promising substantive experience for a bounded refactor, scenario 1 provides the clearest concrete target: convert the tap-to-reveal pot sequence into an actual drag/build interaction, fix the +/- control in 'Build my own,' and add visible feedback to the array-tapping stage. This is a bounded, well-scoped refactor opportunity, whereas scenario 2 requires diagnosing a totally broken state machine with zero information about intended interactions, and scenario 3 requires structurally replacing its entire quiz paradigm with a genuine builder mechanic — a much larger, less bounded rework.
